text:
Sam: FYI spotted small cluster of double-charges for streaming tokens when mobile clients flip from WS -> SSE after NAT churn. looks like two endpoints both accounted for the same replay window.
Priya: can you drop the short trace? curious if resume flow created concurrent owners or if we minted a new session id.
Sam: trace (sanitized):
```
2026-03-22T09:18:01Z INFO conn accepted proto=ws session=zz9 route=us-central-1-a resume_tok=tok:old
2026-03-22T09:18:03Z WARN client-ip-change detected old=1.2.3.4 new=5.6.7.8 landed route=us-central-1-b
2026-03-22T09:18:04Z INFO resume accepted proto=sse session=zz9 route=us-central-1-b resume_tok=tok:old
2026-03-22T09:18:10Z BILL charge route=us-central-1-a session=zz9 tokens=80
2026-03-22T09:18:12Z BILL charge route=us-central-1-b session=zz9 tokens=30
```
Carlos: oof. same session id reused and resume token valid across routes. old route didn't notice the new claim in time and billed its buffered tokens.
Lila: what are current invariants? I thought resume_tokens were opaque but we treat session_id as single-owner. clearly need to make ownership transfer explicit.
Sam: agreed. short-term mitigation options: (a) drop tombstone from 30s -> 2s so old route stops charging quicker, (b) on resume acceptance publish a "session.handoff" event to route-control topic so old-route can immediately revoke billing, or (c) make resume acceptance synchronous call to control plane to revoke ownership (slower path).
Priya: (a) risky for long-tail replays; (c) adds control plane round-trip per resume which hurts tail latency. (b) seems sweet spot if we make the pubsub best-effort + idempotent.
Carlos: implemented a quick PoC for (b) in a tiny canary earlier today: new-route publishes `session.handoff` with {session, new_route, nonce}. old-route subscribes and if it sees a newer nonce it stops billing and marks session handed_off. reduced duplicate charges in canary by ~95%.
Lila: great. telemetry asks: we need a per-tenant `duplicate_stream_charge` metric and a `session_handoff_count` metric, plus a histogram of handoff latency (time from resume accepted to old-route revoke). Console should surface top N affected tenants and show a small timeline for the session illustrating: accept, handoff event, revoke, billing ticks.
Sam: agree. also emit a `resume_token_schema` tag (legacy vs v2) so we can track old tokens. for long term we should include route_tag and handoff_nonce inside tokens so a new-route can detect cross-route resumes and either fast-fail or perform an explicit claim dance.
Priya: rough token v2 sketch: {session_id, issued_route, epoch, handoff_nonce, flags}. If issued_route != current_route and flags.force_claim==false -> reject with 409 resume-claim-required and return claim_nonce. client retries and server publishes claim. This keeps resume acceptance explicit without centralising state.
Carlos: UX note for Console: make the session timeline small and copyable, include a quick button: "request-billing-review" that opens support ticket pre-filled with timeline + charges. helpful for CS to triage double-charge complaints.
Lila: alerting: don't page SRE on every duplicate_stream_charge spike. default to sample and aggregate by tenant; page if a tenant sees sustained >$50 in duplicated tokens over 10m.
infra-bot: canary deploy for session.handoff publisher -> rolled to 8% traffic us-central at 2026-03-22T12:00:00Z. monitoring: duplicate_stream_charge, handoff_latency_p50/p95.
billing-bot: alert: duplicate_stream_charge (sampled) above baseline for us-central -> 2026-03-22T12:06:15Z sample_count=9 top_tenant=acme_inc.
Sam: plan: (1) continue session.handoff canary and gather handoff_latency histogram (Carlos to own), (2) RFC token-v2 doc (Priya to write) for route-affinity+nonce, (3) Console timeline + support-button (Lila to own).
Priya: can we also add a server-side guard for double-billing: when old-route bills tokens it should check control-plane whether session seen handed_off recently and skip billing if so. cheap cache lookup.
Carlos: yes we can make billing path consult an LRU of recent handoffs; TTL 60s. small perf hit but acceptable as a safeguard.
Lila: timeline: canary 24h -> evaluate duplicate metric; if <2% promote. UI beta behind feature flag for a week then enable for ops users.
Sam: thanks team. I'll attach canary traces and a tiny repro harness (simulates client NAT flip between WS/SSE) to the RFC ticket. cc @support-team for the support button UX ideas. :wave:
